source: hand-authored fixture for issue #309 — not shipped data
description: Shapes about whether a CONDITION rule's bare-containment match against a recorded condition is corroborated, for the injected record's patient-specific reading. The recorded condition names are taken from the OpenMRS 3.7.1 reference-application demo dictionary, the corpus issue #309's measurement was run over (the allergen 'Nefotenone' on the Nefopam entry is invented, and is not one of them). (1) Naltrexone rules on the condition token 'liver', which is the most plausible hepatic contraindication token there is and which nests inside every deliver/delivery form the dictionary publishes — 20 of the 30 values it matches over that dictionary's 2581 condition candidates, e.g. 'Status Post Cesarean Delivery'. (2) Acamprosate files the SAME rule as Naltrexone with the token padded ('  liver  '), because the witness filter trims a token and the boundary question must be put to the same string it trimmed — untrimmed, an operator's stray whitespace silently loses the recorded attribution. (3) Metformin rules on 'renal', which nests inside 'Malignant tumor of adrenal gland' — a tumour of a different organ. (4) Ibuprofen rules on 'peptic ulcer', which is one of the four condition tokens the SHIPPED curated seed publishes; over both measured corpora every one of its matches carries it as a whole word, which is the loss side of the boundary rule and is zero. (6) Paracetamol rules on 'edema', whose mid-word matches are clinically RIGHT compounds ('Lymphedema', 'Angioedema') — the residue the boundary rule gives up, kept here so a future change can read what it costs. (5) Nefopam carries NO condition rule and is here for a coverage reason rather than a matching one: it re-pins the `continue` guard in DrugSafetyValidator.addContraindications, whose only previous witness used an unmatched CONDITION rule and which #309's change therefore disarmed — a self-named allergy rule 'nefo' that an allergen recorded as 'Nefotenone' reaches only mid-word, beside a CLASS allergy rule 'nsaid' that the same allergen does not match at all, both carrying ONE note so the two keys render one clause string. An unmatched non-self-named allergy rule still corroborates TRUE unconditionally, which is what makes it a witness the condition leg cannot silence. No entry carries ATC codes or interactions, so no class comparison can chip and every record is the contraindication arms' own.
